- scripts/workspace_init.sh, scripts/run_workspace_hook.sh, scripts/write_guard.sh, scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh, scripts/ledger_emit_substate.sh, scripts/review_agents_md_materiality.sh, scripts/review_filter_uninteresting_files.sh, scripts/review_reject_verify.sh, scripts/post_review_comment.sh, scripts/check_resolver_diff.sh: All instances of PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 <<'PY' or equivalent script file launches in untrusted checkout CWD | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: Host-side Python execution launches inherit the untrusted checkout as the CWD and do not use `-I` (ignore site-packages/user-site) or `-B` (prevent bytecode), allowing import hijacking via `pathlib.py` or `sitecustomize.py`.
  WHY: An attacker can place malicious code in the untrusted checkout that the Python interpreter imports during startup (e.g., via stdlib shadows), granting that code host-level privileges before the script executes.
  RELATED ITEM: Implicit-execution & trust-boundary finding on the same scripts: host-side execution is exposed to the untrusted checkout before credentials can be guarded.
- Requirement: "Fix every instance of each finding's defect class across this project's changes, not only the cited line."
  Expected change site: All sibling scripts in scripts/ (workspace_init.sh, run_workspace_hook.sh, write_guard.sh, review_conflict_resolve.sh, ledger_emit_substate.sh, review_agents_md_materiality.sh, review_filter_uninteresting_files.sh, review_reject_verify.sh, post_review_comment.sh, check_resolver_diff.sh)
  Evidence of absence: The PR diff contains no modifications to these files, which still launch unisolated host-side Python processes.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
